Blanch fresh mushrooms as directed by the seller and rinse before cooking. Thaw pre-cleaned frozen mushrooms in the refrigerator.
Add the mushrooms near the end and cook just until tender; prolonged cooking can make the broth more bitter.
Soft, distinct green rice grains with a gentle lotus-leaf aroma, complemented by nutty beans, lotus seeds and mildly sweet coconut.

Fragrant green young rice is steamed until just tender, then folded with fluffy mung beans, lotus seeds and lightly sweetened coconut. This Bếp Việt home adaptation keeps the grains soft without oversteaming.
Serve warm or slightly cooled, wrapped in a clean lotus leaf or arranged on a small plate. Reduce the sugar to emphasize the rice aroma.
Mung-bean soaking is passive time; steam the rice briefly to preserve its aroma and texture.
young rice with lotus seeds and mung beans
Fresh young rice is usually moist enough; add only a little water if it seems dry.
Steam for about 4–5 minutes, just until warm and tender; longer steaming can make the rice mushy and dull its aroma.
Drain the mung beans well before mashing so they stay fluffy.
Small lightly charred rolls with a soft, chewy rice wrapper and a moist, savory shrimp-and-pork filling; serve with herbs, pickles and dipping sauce.

Fresh shrimp is coarsely pounded and mixed with pork belly, shallot and cut rice noodles, then wrapped in fresh rice sheets and grilled until fragrant and lightly browned. This Bếp Việt home adaptation uses a grill pan or charcoal grill.
Serve hot with fresh herbs, green papaya pickles and sweet-and-sour fish sauce. Grill over charcoal or in a heavy pan.
4 servings, about 3–4 small rolls per person.
Grill in batches over medium heat so the wrappers do not burn before the filling is cooked.
Pound the shrimp in a mortar for a coarse texture; do not blend it into a paste.
Roll snugly so the rice sheet holds the filling without tearing; lightly moisten dry edges.
Grill over medium heat, turning evenly, and cook the shrimp and pork filling through before serving.

names: Phù Mỹ Freshwater Crab Noodle Soup
fields: A hot, fragrant crab broth with naturally set crab meat and roe, served over soft rice vermicelli and balanced with lime, chili and optional herbs.

Fresh field crabs are cleaned, pounded and strained, then gently simmered until their meat and roe set into the rustic broth of Phù Mỹ. This Bếp Việt home adaptation keeps the broth focused on crab and serves herbs on the side according to preference.
Divide the vermicelli into bowls and ladle over gently simmering crab broth. Serve toasted rice crackers, lime, chili and herbs separately; roasted peanuts are optional.
4 bowls, each with about 200 g rice vermicelli and hot crab broth.
Cleaning and pounding the crabs take most of the preparation time; simmer gently to keep the broth clear.
Phù Mỹ Freshwater Crab Noodle Soup
Wash the crabs thoroughly and strain through a fine sieve to remove sand and shell fragments.
Once the broth starts to simmer, avoid vigorous stirring so the crab meat can set.
Cook the crab thoroughly. Sea crab is not a direct substitute because it has a different flavor.

names: Bắc Kạn Tày-Style Bò Khai Greens with Egg
Tày-style stir-fried bò khai with egg
fields: Vivid green, tender-crisp shoots coated with fully cooked egg and fragrant garlic, served hot with steamed rice.
Tày-style stir-fried bò khai with egg

Tender bò khai shoots are snapped into short lengths, quickly stir-fried with garlic and tossed with egg until just cooked. This rustic dish is associated with Tày meals in Bắc Kạn; this Bếp Việt adaptation uses family-sized portions and keeps the greens vivid.
Transfer to a plate as soon as the egg is cooked and serve hot with steamed rice. Add a little chili if desired.
4 rice-meal servings, about 100 g raw bò khai greens per serving.
Drain the greens thoroughly after washing so they stir-fry instead of steaming in the pan.
Bắc Kạn Tày-Style Bò Khai Greens with Egg
Choose young tips, remove tough stems and damaged leaves, then wash and drain thoroughly.
Stir-fry quickly over high heat to preserve the green color and avoid excess liquid.
Cook the egg through; toss just enough for it to coat the greens without becoming dry.

names: Hòa Bình Buffalo Stew with Lá Lồm
fields: Tender, savory buffalo with the gentle sourness of lá lồm and a lightly thickened broth from broken rice, fragrant with ginger and garlic.

Buffalo is cleaned, lightly seared and slowly simmered with pounded lá lồm leaves and broken rice until the broth thickens slightly. This traditional Mường dish from Hòa Bình has a gentle sourness from the leaves; this Bếp Việt home adaptation uses a regular pot.
Ladle hot into deep bowls and serve as a hearty soup in a rice meal. Adjust the salt and sourness after the leaves have softened.
4 bowls served with rice, about 150 g raw buffalo per serving.
Simmering time depends on the toughness of the buffalo cut. If the liquid reduces before the meat is tender, add a little boiling water.
Hòa Bình buffalo lá lồm stew
Hòa Bình Buffalo Stew with Lá Lồm
If the buffalo has a strong aroma, rub it with ginger and rinse before cooking; searing or charring adds fragrance.
Lá lồm is naturally sour; add it gradually to avoid making the stew too tart.
Simmer gently until tender. If using a pressure cooker, follow its timing instructions and release pressure safely before opening.

names: Phú Thọ Sour Cassava-Leaf and Pork Rib Soup
fields: Tender ribs and soft cassava leaves in a gently sour, savory broth with fragrant shallot.

Fermented cassava leaves simmer with pork ribs for a gently sour, earthy soup associated with Phú Thọ home cooking. This Bếp Việt home adaptation keeps the seasoning light so the leaves and rib broth remain distinct.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with steamed rice and a lightly seasoned main dish. Taste only after the leaves soften, since preserved leaves may already be salty.
4 shared bowls for a family meal.
Simmering time varies by rib cut; cook the cassava leaves until tender while keeping their strands intact.
pork rib and fermented cassava leaves
Phú Thọ Sour Cassava-Leaf and Pork Rib Soup
Use properly prepared, fermented cassava leaves; never use raw leaves.
Squeeze out some brine and taste before rinsing so the leaves do not become bland.
Season with salt or fish sauce at the end because preserved leaves can already be salty.

names: Trà Vinh Cháo Ám Snakehead Fish Porridge
fields: A gently thick porridge fragrant with fish and dried seafood, with tender snakehead, soft fish roe and crisp fresh greens.

Snakehead fish cooking broth becomes the base for rice porridge, enriched with boneless fish, dried shrimp and toasted dried squid. The Trà Vinh-style bowl is served with fresh greens, peanuts and a savory chili bean dip.

Ladle the hot porridge into bowls and top with fish, scallion and cilantro. Serve with blanched bean sprouts, bitter greens, shredded banana blossom, sesame rice crackers and a bean-sauce dip seasoned with fermented fish sauce, lime and chili to taste.
4 bowls of snakehead fish porridge, served hot with fresh greens and dipping sauce.
Cooking time depends on the rice; stir the bottom of the pot regularly to prevent sticking.
Trà Vinh Cháo Ám Snakehead Fish Porridge
Strain the fish broth before cooking the rice to remove small bones.
Flake the fish while warm and check carefully for remaining bones.
If fish roe is unavailable, omit it; chicken egg would change the dish’s character.

names: Cà Mau Stir-Fried Bồn Bồn with Dried Shrimp
fields: Ivory-white, crisp bồn bồn shoots coated with savory dried shrimp and fragrant shallot, without excess liquid.

Tender bồn bồn shoots stay crisp and sweet when quickly stir-fried over high heat with dried shrimp and shallot. This simple vegetable dish is associated with Cà Mau; the Bếp Việt adaptation keeps the sauce light so the vegetable remains the focus.
Serve as soon as the stir-fry is done, finished with black pepper and steamed rice. Add a little lime if you prefer a brighter flavor.
4 portions of lightly crisp stir-fried vegetables to serve with rice.
Total time excludes soaking the dried shrimp; stir-fry the shoots briefly to retain their crunch.
stir-fried cattail shoots with dried shrimp
Cà Mau Stir-Fried Bồn Bồn with Dried Shrimp
Use tender inner bồn bồn shoots and trim any tough ends; soak briefly in light salt water.
Drain thoroughly before stir-frying so the shoots do not steam and soften.
Cook quickly over high heat without covering the pan.

names: Huế Tapioca Dumpling and Roasted Pork Sweet Soup
fields: Soft, chewy, slightly translucent dumplings with a savory-sweet roasted pork center in fragrant ginger syrup that is not overly sweet.

Chewy, translucent tapioca dumplings enclose pork roasted and gently candied with rock sugar, then simmer in a light ginger syrup. This Bếp Việt home adaptation moderates the sweetness so the savory, rich filling remains clear, reflecting Huế’s distinctive sweet-and-savory dessert.
Spoon a few dumplings and ginger syrup into small bowls and finish with roasted peanuts. Serve warm for the ginger aroma or over ice for a cool dessert.
6 small bowls, served warm or chilled.
Total time varies with the water temperature and amount used to knead the dough; this recipe starts with cooked roast pork.
Huế tapioca dumplings with roasted pork
sweet soup with savory pork filling
Huế Tapioca Dumpling and Roasted Pork Sweet Soup
Dice the roast pork finely and trim away any overly tough skin so the filling is easy to wrap.
Knead the tapioca starch with hot water gradually, stopping when the dough is pliable and no longer sticky.
Once the dumplings float, simmer them for a few more minutes so the dough cooks evenly around the filling.

names: Hmong Mèn Mén from former Hà Giang
fields: Soft, fluffy grains of steamed corn with a naturally nutty aroma and no added seasoning.

Mèn mén is a traditional steamed corn dish of the Hmong people on the Đồng Văn Karst Plateau in former Hà Giang, now part of Tuyên Quang. Finely milled field corn is moistened, loosened and steamed twice, with the mixture fluffed between rounds so it cooks evenly. This Bếp Việt home version uses ready-ground cornmeal.
Serve hot with vegetable or bean soup; a separately served braise can accompany it for a non-vegetarian meal. The mèn mén itself keeps the natural flavor of corn.
4 portions of steamed ground field corn, served as the meal’s staple.
Traditional preparation can take 2–3 hours; this estimate assumes the corn is already milled and varies with grind size.
Hmong mèn mén from former Hà Giang province
Hmong Mèn Mén from former Hà Giang
Use finely milled field corn and sift out any hard hull pieces; do not use precooked instant polenta.
Sprinkle water in gradually and rub the meal until loose like damp sand, avoiding large clumps.
Steam twice and fluff the grains between rounds; water and timing depend on the grind and maturity of the corn.

names: Red jellyfish salad with shrimp sauce
fields: Crispy jellyfish, fragrant yellow tofu, lightly sweet coconut flesh; The vegetables stay fresh and the salty and sour dipping sauce is just right.
Red jellyfish salad with shrimp sauce

Hai Phong red jellyfish salad stands out with crispy pink jellyfish, served with turmeric grilled tofu, coconut meat, herbs and a bowl of shrimp paste or vinegar. Viet Kitchen edits family-oriented recipes, using pre-processed and safely packaged jellyfish; Do not handle fresh, unprocessed jellyfish yourself.
Arrange jellyfish and side dishes separately on a plate. Roll each portion with perilla leaves, marjoram or fig leaves, dip in shrimp paste mixed with vinegar; Clean up immediately after mixing.
4 portions of red jellyfish salad rolled with herbs, coconut meat, grilled tofu and rice paper.
About 40 minutes if using prepared jellyfish; Time may vary according to instructions on packaging.
Red jellyfish dipped in shrimp paste
Only buy properly processed red jellyfish from a trustworthy facility; Do not use fresh jellyfish caught yourself.
Drain the jellyfish thoroughly before serving so that the dish does not become watery.
Grill the tofu until golden brown, keeping the inside soft; Mix your own dipping sauce so everyone can add some.

names: Hai Phong shrimp and celery vermicelli
fields: The broth is fragrant with shrimp and has a mild taste; Firmly cooked shrimp, lightly crispy wood ear mushrooms and just-cooked celery.
Hai Phong shrimp and celery vermicelli

Hai Phong shrimp vermicelli has a sweet clear broth from shrimp bones and heads, accompanied by stir-fried shrimp, wood ear mushrooms, celery, tomatoes and dill. Viet Kitchen compiles the right amount of spices for home meals; Keep both whole shrimp and minced shrimp so that the bowl of vermicelli has many layers of flavor.
Blanch the noodles, place the shrimp and celery in a bowl and pour in the hot broth. Sprinkle with green onions, dill, and pepper; Serve lemon and chili separately.
4 bowls of shrimp vermicelli with bone broth and fresh water filtered from shrimp heads.
About 1 hour and 15 minutes, including time to simmer the broth.
Stir-fry the shrimp heads and shells until fragrant, then filter carefully so the broth is fragrant without being lumpy.
Do not cook celery for long; Blanch quickly to preserve color and crispness.
If using fish sauce with high saltiness, season after the broth has thickened.

names: Nha Trang Jellyfish and Ca Liet Fish Vermicelli Soup
Jellyfish and ca liet fish vermicelli soup
Nha Trang ca liet fish vermicelli soup
fields: The clear broth is gently sweet from ca liet fish. Crisp jellyfish, picked fish and tender-chewy sea fish cake are served with vermicelli and fresh herbs.
Jellyfish and ca liet fish vermicelli soup
Nha Trang ca liet fish vermicelli soup

Nha Trang jellyfish vermicelli soup has a clear broth made from ca liet fish, with picked fish meat, sea fish cake and crisp prepared jellyfish. Serve with fresh rice vermicelli, bean sprouts and herbs; offer fermented fish sauce, lime and chili on the side.

Place vermicelli, jellyfish, picked fish and sea fish cake in a bowl; pour over hot ca liet fish broth and add bean sprouts, scallions and cilantro. Serve fermented fish sauce, lime and chili separately.
Four bowls of jellyfish vermicelli soup with ca liet fish, sea fish cake, clear broth and fresh greens.
Editorial estimate; actual timing depends on fish, prepared jellyfish and equipment.
Nha Trang jellyfish and ca liet fish vermicelli soup
jellyfish vermicelli with ca liet broth
Nha Trang Jellyfish and Ca Liet Fish Vermicelli Soup
Use food-grade prepared jellyfish and follow the package directions before serving.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer and skim it to maintain a clear finish.
Season fermented fish sauce separately so each diner can adjust the bowl.

names: Banh xeo filled with coconut tubers
Banh xeo with shrimp and coconut in Ben Tre
fields: The crust is thin and crispy on the edges, the shrimp and meat are just cooked and the coconut tub is still crispy; The accompanying vegetables make the cake taste lighter.
Banh xeo filled with coconut tubers
Banh xeo with shrimp and coconut in Ben Tre

Ben Tre coconut tofu pancake combines a crispy golden rice crust with sweet, crispy young coconut tofu, shrimp and pork belly; Coconut milk makes the dough fragrant and light. Viet Kitchen edited the family recipe, kept coconut tubers as the highlight and served with garden vegetables and sweet and sour fish sauce.
Fold the cake into half moons, serve hot with lettuce, herbs and a cup of sweet and sour fish sauce. Roll each piece with vegetables to balance out the fatty taste.
4 medium-sized pancakes filled with shrimp, meat and coconut tubers, served with raw vegetables.
About 1 hour, including time to prepare and pour each cake.
Let the dough rest for at least 15 minutes then stir again before pouring.
Coconut tubers should be cut thinly so they cook quickly but are still crispy.
Preheat the pan, coat with a thin layer of dough and don't pour too much filling to keep the edges crispy.

names: Herring salad rolled with rice paper
fields: Cool fish with lemon flavor, lightly fatty shredded coconut, fragrant wild vegetables and sweet and sour fish sauce create a well-balanced salad.
Herring salad rolled with rice paper

Phu Quoc herring salad is a dish of lime fish rolled with rice paper with wild vegetables, star fruit, shredded coconut and peanuts, dipped in fish sauce mixed with garlic and chili. Viet Kitchen edits meals at home and adds instructions for choosing and keeping fish safely refrigerated; Lemon juice does not replace parasite control procedures for raw fish.

Place the fish pieces on coconut oil rice paper, add vegetables, star fruit, shredded coconut and roasted peanuts, roll up and dip in sweet and sour fish sauce. Serve the fish cold and eat immediately after mixing.
4 portions of herring salad with lemon, rolled with wild vegetables, shredded coconut and rice paper.
About 55 minutes, including preparing and briefly cooling the fish before serving.
fish salad rolled with rice paper
Use only fish from controlled sources, clearly marketed for raw consumption; Keep refrigerated continuously and prepare with clean utensils.
Lemon juice creates a bland taste but does not reliably eliminate bacteria or parasites; Pregnant people, young children, the elderly or immunocompromised should choose cooked fish.
Roll coconut oil rice paper without dipping in water; If the rice paper is dry and hard, soften it according to the manufacturer's instructions.

names: Phan Thiet Lau Tha Hot Pot
fields: A fragrant shrimp broth with gentle acidity from tomato and pineapple; ca mai, pork, egg and greens are arranged separately for cooking at the table.
Lam Dong (Phan Thiet, former Binh Thuan Province)
A Phan Thiet hot pot centered on fresh ca mai and a colorful spread of accompaniments. This Bep Viet home version serves it with a light shrimp, tomato and pineapple broth.

Arrange vermicelli, greens, cucumber, pork, egg and ca mai on separate plates. Once the broth boils, cook the fish until opaque, then eat with noodles and greens; add a little sweet-and-sour sauce and roasted peanuts.
Four servings, with ca mai, vermicelli and greens arranged separately around a pot of hot broth.
Keep ca mai chilled after cleaning and cook it in the boiling broth before eating.
Phan Thiet ca mai lau tha
ca mai with vermicelli and herbs
Phan Thiet Lau Tha Hot Pot
Choose very fresh ca mai, clean it thoroughly and keep it chilled; use a separate board and knife for raw fish.
Bring the broth to a steady boil before serving so the fish can cook through when dipped.
Add the dipping sauce gradually so it does not overpower the fish and greens.

names: Ca Mau Water-Sprite Shoots Stir-Fried with Tiny Shrimp
U Minh water-sprite shoots with tiny shrimp
fields: Fresh green, lightly crisp shoots coated with sweet shrimp, fragrant garlic and a touch of pepper.
U Minh water-sprite shoots with tiny shrimp

Young, lightly curled water-sprite shoots are quickly stir-fried with tiny shrimp, garlic and seasoning. Tuoi Tre identifies this as a common preparation in the U Minh area; Bep Viet standardizes the amounts for a family meal.
Serve hot with steamed rice. A small bowl of gently sweet, sour and spicy fish sauce is an optional accompaniment.
One family-style dish for four, served with rice.
Prepare the greens and shrimp before heating the wok; quick stir-frying helps retain the young shoots' texture.
rau choai from the Mekong Delta
Ca Mau shrimp and greens stir-fry
Ca Mau Water-Sprite Shoots Stir-Fried with Tiny Shrimp
Choose fresh young shoots and remove old leaves and fibrous stems.
Add the shoots as soon as the shrimp turn golden and stir-fry briefly to retain their texture.
If the shoots are very mucilaginous, blanch them quickly and drain thoroughly before stir-frying.

names: Cao Bang Banh Khao (Pressed Glutinous Rice Cakes)
fields: Small ivory-colored cakes with fragrant, airy toasted-rice flour and a lightly sweet filling of peanuts, sesame and pork fat.

banh khao is a Lunar New Year cake associated with the Tay and Nung communities of Cao Bang, made from finely milled toasted glutinous rice with a filling of peanuts, sesame and pork fat. This Bep Viet home adaptation rests the pressed cakes in a clean lined mold.
Let the cakes set in the mold, then release and cut into small pieces. Serve with hot tea and store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place.
About 12 small cakes, two or three pieces per person.
Cool the toasted rice fully before grinding. The amount of water depends on how dry the flour is, so add it gradually.
Tay and Nung banh khao from Cao Bang
banh khao with peanut and sesame filling
Cao Bang Lunar New Year cake
Cao Bang Banh Khao (Pressed Glutinous Rice Cakes)
Toast the glutinous rice over low heat, stirring continuously so it turns aromatic without darkening.
Mill the rice very finely and sift it for a smooth, compact cake.
Rest the cakes in a clean mold lined with food-safe paper; never place the flour directly on the floor.

names: Ninh Binh Crispy Rice with Goat Sauce
Ninh Binh crispy rice with goat meat sauce
fields: A golden, airy rice cake topped with lightly thickened goat sauce, tomato and mushrooms; the meat is tender and fragrant with ginger and lemongrass.
Ninh Binh crispy rice with goat meat sauce

Ninh Binh crispy rice has a golden, crunchy crust formed in a thick-bottomed pot; it may be served with pork floss or goat sauce. This Bep Viet version pairs it with a family-style tomato and mushroom goat sauce.
Spoon only enough hot goat sauce over the crispy rice just before eating to keep the exposed surface crisp. Serve hot with herbs or pickled vegetables.
Four servings, each with a crisp rice cake and hot goat sauce.
Air-drying time varies with rice-cake thickness and humidity; the crust should feel dry before frying.
Ninh Binh crispy rice with goat sauce
Ninh Binh Crispy Rice with Goat Sauce
Use a cast-iron or heavy-bottomed pot and keep the rice layer thin so the crust browns evenly.
Dry the rice crust before frying; this helps it puff and reduces oil splatter.
Add the sauce just before serving to keep the rice crisp.

names: Ngu Xa Pho Rolls from Ha Noi
fields: Soft white pho sheets filled with fragrant garlic beef, lettuce and herbs, served with balanced sweet-and-sour dipping sauce.

Wide pho sheets wrap stir-fried beef and fresh herbs, served with sweet-and-sour fish sauce. This well-known Ngu Xa, Ha Noi dish is adapted by Bep Viet with home-friendly amounts and a compact filling so the rolls stay neat.
Arrange the rolls on a platter with a bowl of sweet-and-sour fish sauce with garlic and chili. Serve while the beef is aromatic and the pho sheets are soft.
About 16 rolls, suitable for four light servings or two to three main-meal servings.
Let the beef cool slightly before rolling; very hot or wet filling can tear the soft pho sheets.
Ngu Xa Pho Rolls from Ha Noi
Choose wide pho sheets that are soft but not overly wet so the rolls hold their shape.
Let the beef cool slightly before rolling to keep the pho sheets from tearing.
Do not overfill; place the greens in the middle and roll snugly.

names: Quang Ngai Tra River Goby Braised with Pepper
Tra River goby braised with pepper
fields: Whole gobies are firm and peppery, coated in a light glossy sauce fragrant with shallot.
Tra River goby braised with pepper

Small gobies simmer gently with fish sauce, black pepper and a little chili until firm and glazed. Bếp Việt edits this home-style version for a family meal, keeping the Tra River specialty's peppery aroma and balanced savory-sweet finish.
Serve hot with steamed rice and boiled greens; spoon a little braising sauce over the rice.
One small pot of fish served with steamed rice for four.
Smaller fish absorb seasoning quickly; avoid reducing the sauce until dry so the fish stays moist.
Quang Ngai Tra River Goby Braised with Pepper
Choose fresh small gobies; rinse gently and drain well so they stay intact.
Season with fish sauce early, then taste near the end because the sauce will reduce.
Braise over low heat and gently shake the pot instead of stirring.
Soft rice grains in a lightly thickened broth, with plump oysters and fragrant pepper and herbs.
Ho Chi Minh City (including former Ba Ria - Vung Tau Province)

Rice simmers into lightly creamy porridge; oysters are briefly sautéed and added near the end to preserve their briny sweetness. Fried shallot, scallion, cilantro and pepper make a warming bowl; Bếp Việt edits this for home cooking.
Ladle into bowls and finish with fried shallot, scallion, cilantro and pepper; thinly sliced banana blossom is optional.
Simmering time varies by rice; add oysters near the end and cook through without overcooking.
Use cleaned oysters kept properly chilled, and cook through.
Sauté oysters just until firm and add near the end to avoid a rubbery texture.
Add hot water if porridge thickens, and stir the bottom regularly.

names: Vegetarian Braised Young Jackfruit with Straw Mushrooms
Young jackfruit braised with mushrooms and tofu
fields: Tender jackfruit with sweet mushrooms and tofu in a lightly reduced lemongrass sauce.
Young jackfruit braised with mushrooms and tofu

Tender young jackfruit is braised with straw mushrooms and tofu in soy, lemongrass and vegetarian fish-sauce broth. Bếp Việt edits this home version so the sauce reduces lightly while ingredients keep their shape.
Serve with rice and cilantro or leek greens. Check seasonings are plant-based for a fully vegan meal.
One shared braise for a four-person meal.
Fresh and pre-cooked jackfruit vary in tenderness; adjust timing so pieces do not break apart.
Vegetarian Braised Young Jackfruit with Straw Mushrooms
If fresh jackfruit is sticky with latex, boil it for 5 minutes and drain before pan-frying.
Briefly pan-frying jackfruit and tofu helps the pieces hold their shape.
Use vegetarian fish sauce; do not use regular fish sauce for a vegetarian meal.

names: Northern Vietnamese grilled fish with galangal and fermented rice
Grilled carp with galangal and fermented rice
fields: Golden grilled carp with a fragrant galangal and lemongrass crust, tender flesh, gentle tang from fermented rice and optional chili heat.
Grilled carp with galangal and fermented rice

Carp is marinated with galangal, lemongrass, turmeric and fermented rice, then grilled until fragrant and golden while the flesh stays moist. This Northern Vietnamese home-style dish is served with herbs and a dipping sauce.
Serve hot with steamed rice or vermicelli, fresh herbs and a sweet-sour fish sauce dip with garlic and chili.
One fish around 900 g, divided among four and served with rice or vermicelli and fresh herbs.
Marinate the fish under refrigeration. Grilling time is an estimate and varies with fish size, oven and charcoal heat.
Northern Vietnamese grilled fish with galangal and fermented rice
Score the fish shallowly on both sides so the marinade reaches the flesh and it grills evenly.
Marinate in the refrigerator for at least one hour; do not leave raw fish at room temperature for an extended period.
Grilling time varies with fish size and equipment; check the thickest part is cooked before serving.

names: Quang Nam Banh Thuan Flower Cakes
fields: Pale golden cakes bloom into petals, smell of egg and have a lightly dry exterior with an airy crumb.
Da Nang City (including former Quang Nam Province)

Quang Nam banh thuan has flower-like petals and fragrant egg aroma, traditionally made for Tet, family rites and guests. Bếp Việt edits a small home batch with arrowroot starch, eggs and sugar baked in a small mold; texture varies with starch and mold.
Cool on a rack and serve with hot tea; store airtight once completely cool.
About 12 small cakes, depending on mold size.
This small-batch home method is an adaptation; traditional molds and starch types can produce different textures.
Quang Nam Banh Thuan Flower Cakes
Sift arrowroot starch and beat eggs thoroughly for a smooth batter.
Preheat mold and brush lightly with oil so petals form cleanly.
When using an oven instead of the traditional mold, test a small batch because mold and heat affect rise.

names: Cao Bang Black Canarium Sticky Rice
Cao Bang Glutinous Rice with Black Canarium
ingredients: Yellow Flower glutinous rice or upland sticky rice
fields: Sticky rice seeds are soft and naturally pink and purple; The meat is soft and fleshy, has a mild sour taste and a characteristic aroma.
Cao Bang Glutinous Rice with Black Canarium

Cao Bang black canarium sticky rice is an autumn specialty: softened black canarium flesh is pitted and folded into hot sticky rice, coloring the grains mauve and adding a gentle, nutty richness. Bep Viet adapts it for a family-sized batch and keeps the fruit-softening step separate to prevent a tough or astringent result.
Serve hot in a bowl or tray lined with clean leaves. You can sprinkle sesame salt or roasted peanuts; Traditional dishes can also be eaten with minced meat depending on the region and taste.
4 servings of black sticky rice, served hot; Can be used with sesame salt.
About 9 hours and 25 minutes, mostly soaking time; Can be prepared the night before.
sticky rice filled with sticky rice
Cao Bang Black Canarium Sticky Rice
Priority should be given to filling with ripe sticky rice, fresh fruit and taut skin; Plain fillings are usually harder.
Just braise the fillings in hot water, do not boil; Separate the seeds when the pulp is just soft.
Drain the sticky rice before cooking and keep the heat steady so the grains cook evenly.
Vegetarian dishes depending on how you use them
Yellow Flower glutinous rice or upland sticky rice

names: Lang Son Khau Nhuc (Braised Pork Belly Dome)
fields: The pork belly is soft and absorbent, the shiny brown skin, the fleshy taro and the fragrant salty shrimp create a bold but round flavor.

Khau nhuc, also called nam khau, is a labor-intensive steamed dish associated with the Tay and Nung communities of Lang Son, often served for family celebrations and weddings. Bep Viet adapts the process for a home kitchen: brown the pork skin, layer the pork with taro and preserved mustard greens, then steam slowly until tender.
Place the steaming bowl on a deep plate, sprinkle the steaming liquid on top and serve hot with white rice, bread or boiled vegetables.
The 6 parts include steamed pork belly, taro and seasoned pork belly.
About 6:15 a.m.; Mostly slow steaming time to soften the meat.
Lang Son Khau Nhuc (Braised Pork Belly Dome)
Choose pork belly with balanced layers of lean, fat and skin; Prick the skin evenly to let the seasoning absorb.
Pat the skin dry before sautéing; Place the skin side down in the hot oil and cover to avoid splashing.
Chinese soi is quite salty, so taste it before adding salt or soy sauce; Steam over low heat and add hot water as needed.
Hot fish smells of roasted mushrooms and guava leaves, firm fibers, mild sour and salty taste; Grill until the fish is not dry.

Lap Thach fermented fish is a traditional way of preserving fish from the Lo River with salt, toasted corn meal and guava leaves, producing a distinctive tangy aroma. Bep Viet adapts it as a quick grilled dish and uses only fully fermented fish from a trusted producer; it does not provide instructions for fermenting raw fish at home.
Grill thoroughly, remove the meat and eat with white rice, herbs and cucumbers. Do not eat raw or undercooked fish.
4 portions of fish are completely fermented, grilled and eaten with hot rice.
About 32 minutes if using fully fermented fish; Traditional incubation times are not included in this recipe.
Choose fish products with clear labels, origin and preservation instructions.
Do not ferment raw fish at home without procedures to control salt, temperature and time.
If the fish is salty, serve with rice and boiled vegetables; No need to add salty dipping sauce.
The cake crust is clear and golden; The green bean filling is soft and fleshy, with grated coconut and fragrant lotus seeds.

Dinh Bang husband-and-wife cake is known for its translucent golden glutinous-rice shell, lightly crisp green papaya strands and sweet mung-bean and coconut filling. Bep Viet adapts a small home batch while retaining the traditional two-layer leaf wrapping and natural gardenia coloring.
Let the cake cool down, then serve it whole or cut it in half to reveal the clear crust and filling. Store cool in an airtight container and use within a day.
6 husband and wife cakes wrapped in leaves, used as sweets or holiday gifts.
About 2 hours 35 minutes, not including time for cake to cool completely.
Dinh Bang bride and groom cake
Squeeze out the water from the papaya after grating it so that the skin doesn't become mushy.
Stir the flour continuously over low heat until it thickens, avoiding the bottom of the pot being sharp.
Wrap the leaves tightly in your hand, do not press too tightly so that the dough has room to expand when steamed.

names: Vegetarian Sang Greens and Mushroom Soup
fields: Clear, sweet soup from mushrooms; Soft green spinach leaves, tofu and mushrooms create a light feeling in the stomach.
Vegetarian Sang Greens and Mushroom Soup

Sang greens are a forest vegetable associated with Xuan Son, Phu Tho, with tender young leaves and a naturally sweet finish; local versions are cooked with pork, shrimp or fish. Bep Viet offers a clearly labeled vegetarian adaptation with mushrooms and tofu, letting the greens remain the main flavor.
Ladle the soup while it's still hot, serve with white rice and vegetarian stew. Do not boil vegetables for long to preserve color and tenderness.
4 bowls of vegetable soup with mushrooms in the vegetarian version edited by Bep Viet.
About 33 minutes, cook quickly so the vegetables retain their green color and sweetness.
Only pick or buy vegetables of clear origin; Choose young leaves, avoid mixing with unidentified forest trees.
Wash gently several times and drain; The old stems can be put in the pot before the leaves.
Season with soy sauce or salt moderately to not overwhelm the natural sweetness of the vegetables and mushrooms.

names: Thach Xa ginger and molasses rice cake
fields: Chewy, firm pieces lightly dusted with rice flour; molasses sweetness is balanced by warm ginger and nutty peanuts.
Thach Xa ginger and molasses rice cake

Che lam from Thach Xa is a Xu Doai sweet made with toasted glutinous rice flour, sugarcane molasses, ginger and roasted peanuts. Bếp Việt has edited a small home batch with a balanced chew and gentle warmth; it is not presented as an artisan household’s exact formula.
Let the cake cool completely, cut into bite-size pieces and serve with green or hot tea.
About 24 chewy pieces served with hot tea.
About 1 hour, including cooling before cutting.
Add toasted rice flour gradually so the mixture stays chewy rather than dry and crumbly.
Cook molasses over low heat, stirring constantly to prevent scorching.
Fold in the peanuts last to keep them crisp.

names: Ha Tinh dried sweet potato and sticky rice
fields: Soft dried sweet potato and sticky rice combine with beans and peanuts for a gently sweet, nutty dish that is not mushy.
Ha Tinh dried sweet potato and sticky rice

Khoai xeo is a rustic Ha Tinh dish made with dried sweet potato, sticky rice, beans and peanuts. Bếp Việt has edited a home method that soaks dry beans first, then gently mashes the cooked mixture so it stays chewy and textured.
Serve warm as breakfast or a snack; add a little sesame-peanut salt if desired.
One pot of chewy, nutty khoai xeo for four people.
About 7 hours 10 minutes, mostly for soaking the beans; soak them overnight if convenient.
Soak dry beans and cook until tender before adding the rice.
Keep the water just level with the ingredients after adding rice; add hot water little by little if needed.
Mash lightly while hot, leaving some sweet potato pieces and beans intact.

names: Yen Tu Bamboo Shoots Stir-Fried with Beef
Yen Tu bamboo shoot and beef stir-fry
Quang Ninh bamboo shoots with beef
fields: Crisp-tender bamboo shoots carry gentle bitterness and sweetness; just-cooked beef is coated with garlic fragrance and a light pan sauce.
Yen Tu bamboo shoot and beef stir-fry
Quang Ninh bamboo shoots with beef

Firm Yen Tu bamboo shoots have a lightly bitter, nutty character and are commonly stir-fried with beef, garlic and seasoning. Bếp Việt has edited a home version that cooks fresh bamboo shoots thoroughly first and keeps the beef tender.
Serve immediately with steamed rice; fresh washed greens may accompany it as in local meals.
One plate of bamboo shoots and beef for four, served with rice.
About 50 minutes, including 10 minutes to marinate the beef and prepare the shoots.
Fresh bamboo shoots must be prepared and boiled thoroughly before stir-frying; never taste them raw.
Quickly sear the beef in a hot pan, remove it, and return it at the end to keep it tender.
Season lightly because the pan juices concentrate as they reduce.

names: Thai-Style Canh Ot from Western Nghe An
ingredients: Young mac khen leaves or fresh herbs
fields: The soup is lightly thickened by softened rice, with tender chicken, delicate young banana pith and fragrant lemongrass.

Canh ột is a rice-and-herb soup of Thai communities in western Nghe An, with variations named for their main ingredient. Bếp Việt has edited a chicken version for home cooking with young banana pith, lemongrass and soaked, coarsely pounded rice; it is not claimed as a universal village recipe.
Serve hot with rice or as the main soup in a meal; offer chili salt separately.
One lightly thickened chicken and rice soup for four people.
About 3 hours 10 minutes, including the rice soak.
Soak and coarsely pound the rice so it thickens the soup without forming lumps.
Cook the chicken fully before adding rice; stir the bottom of the pot as the rice softens.
Use clean young banana pith, remove mature layers and soak briefly in lightly salted water.
Young mac khen leaves or fresh herbs
The fish is fully cooked with lightly charred skin, firm sweet flesh and a fragrant aroma.

Ca mat from the Song Giang River is associated with Muong Qua in western Nghe An. Local reporting describes gentle cleaning followed by grilling, frying, boiling or braising; Bếp Việt has edited a simple grilled home version and does not claim it is the only traditional or ceremonial recipe.
Serve hot with steamed rice, boiled greens and a small bowl of green chili salt.
One plate of grilled ca mat for four people, served with rice and greens.
About 50 minutes, including a 10-minute light seasoning rest.
Choose fresh fish, keep it chilled and prepare it shortly before cooking.
Grill over medium heat and turn gently to cook evenly without breaking the fish.
Cook until the thickest part is opaque and fully done; do not serve raw or undercooked fish.
The pastry is golden and crisp, with a soft pork, mushroom and noodle filling and a quail egg inside.

Hanoi bánh gối is a crisp, pillow-shaped pastry filled with minced pork, wood-ear mushroom, glass noodles and quail egg. This Bếp Việt home batch cools and drains the filling before sealing and frying.
Serve hot with fresh greens, green papaya pickles and sweet-sour fish sauce.
About 8 pork-filled pastries served with fresh greens and dipping sauce.
About 1 hour 10 minutes, including 20 minutes for the dough to rest.
wood-ear mushroom and glass noodle pastry
Cool and drain the filling before wrapping.
Seal the edges firmly; dab dry pastry with a little water.
Fry over medium heat so the shell crisps while the filling cooks through.

names: Hanoi Rice Noodle Soup with Taro Stems
fields: The broth is clear and balanced; the pork is tender, the meatballs savory and the taro stems crisp without an itchy afterfeel.

This Hanoi bowl pairs a light broth with tender pork hock, wood-ear meatballs and crisp taro stems. Bếp Việt’s home recipe explains how to salt, squeeze and rinse the stems to reduce their itchy sensation.
Briefly blanch the noodles, arrange the pork and meatballs, ladle over hot broth and finish with scallion, culantro and cilantro.
Four bowls of rice noodles with pork, meatballs and clear broth.
A gentle simmer keeps the broth clear; salt and rinse the taro stems thoroughly before cooking.
Hanoi Rice Noodle Soup with Taro Stems
Wear gloves when handling taro stems if your skin is sensitive; salt, squeeze and rinse them several times.
Blanch the bones and pork hock before simmering, and skim regularly for a clear broth.
Blanch the taro stems only until just tender; prolonged cooking removes their crisp texture.

names: Giong Luong Coconut Leaf Cake from Ben Tre
fields: Golden-green leaves enclose tender sticky rice with nutty black beans, ripe banana and a gentle coconut aroma.

Giong Luong cake is wrapped in young nipa palm leaves and combines chewy sticky rice with coconut, black beans and ripe banana. Bếp Việt adapts the long-standing Thạnh Phú craft for a small home batch; wrapping and extended steaming take patience.
Let the parcels cool slightly, unwrap and serve whole or sliced; best eaten the day they are made.
This recipe keeps the extended steaming time documented for the traditional craft; actual time varies with parcel thickness.
Ben Tre nipa palm leaf cake
Giong Luong Coconut Leaf Cake from Ben Tre
Soak the sticky rice long enough and drain it thoroughly so the cake cooks chewy rather than wet.
Wipe the young nipa leaves clean, roll them into sealed tubes and tie firmly to keep water out.
Steam for the full time; for larger or thicker parcels, check the center before turning off the heat.

names: Quan Ganh savory banh day with pork filling
fields: Smooth, chewy white sticky rice surrounds a nutty mung-bean and savory pork filling with a light banana-leaf aroma.
Quan Ganh savory banh day with pork filling
Quán Gánh bánh dày is a well-known sticky-rice cake from Thường Tín, Hanoi. This Bếp Việt savory version combines pounded sticky rice with mung bean and pork filling, wrapped in banana leaf.
Serve warm or at room temperature; unwrap the banana leaf to eat.
Eight savory bánh dày cakes wrapped in banana leaf, for four people.
About 5 hours 20 minutes, mostly soaking time for rice and beans.
Soak the rice thoroughly and pound it while hot so it binds.
Oil your hands lightly to prevent sticking.

names: Northern Vietnamese Rice Balls with Sesame Salt
fields: The rice holds together while staying soft and chewy; the sesame salt is fragrant, nutty and mildly salty, with optional roasted peanuts.

Warm rice is pressed into a tender, chewy roll and served with nutty toasted sesame salt, a humble countryside food from northern Vietnam. Bếp Việt keeps the method simple and explains how to cook rice that binds well and shape it while warm.
Slice the rice roll with a slightly wet knife or clean thread and dip into sesame salt while still warm.
Four servings of rice balls with sesame salt, for breakfast or a packed meal.
Rice-cooking time varies by grain and cooker; avoid shaping the rice while it is too hot to handle safely.
Northern Vietnamese Rice Balls with Sesame Salt
Choose a moderately sticky rice and cook it so it is neither dry nor mushy.
Shape the rice while warm using a clean cloth or food-safe plastic wrap.
Toast sesame over low heat, stirring constantly; turn off the heat as soon as fragrant to prevent bitterness.
The cake is golden and crispy at the edges, the middle is soft and fragrant with rice flour; The goby fish is cooked to perfection, with a natural sweetness mixed with bean sprouts and onions.

This Hue lagoon specialty pairs small rabbitfish with a thin rice-flour batter, bean sprouts and scallions. Bep Viet adapts it for a family kitchen, keeping the fish at the center and seasoning it lightly to accompany the dipping sauce.
Serve immediately while the cake is still hot with washed raw vegetables. Can be served with chili garlic fish sauce or thick Hue-style dipping sauce; Season separately to taste.
4 small cakes, served hot with raw vegetables and dipping sauce.
Frying time depends on the thickness of the cake and the size of the fish; Make sure the fish is completely cooked before serving.
Choose a small, firm-bodied orca; Clean the gills and intestines, pat dry before sauteing.
Mix enough flour to cover the bottom of the pan in a thin layer so that the cake is crispy but not crumbly.
Only add the bean sprouts at the end and cover briefly so that the bean sprouts are just hot and don't release too much juice.
Golden grilled skewers smell of lemongrass and remain tender; serve with herbs, green banana, cucumber, noodles and dipping sauce.

Huế nem lụi are seasoned ground meat wrapped around lemongrass stalks and grilled, commonly eaten as rolls with rice paper, noodles and herbs. This Bếp Việt batch adds shrimp and pork fat for a juicy texture.
Wrap a skewer, noodles and herbs in rice paper, then dip in sauce.
About 12 nem lụi skewers served with rice vermicelli and fresh herbs.
About 3 hours 55 minutes, including 3 hours of chilling time.
Knead the mixture until sticky so it adheres to the lemongrass.
Chill the mixture so it absorbs seasoning and is easier to shape.
Turn the skewers halfway through grilling for even browning.
The eggplant is soft but still in pieces, the tofu is soaked in soy sauce, the stock is light and fragrant with pepper.

Tender eggplant and lightly fried tofu are gently braised with soy sauce and black pepper for an easy, home-style vegetarian meal. Bep Viet keeps the braising liquid light enough to coat the ingredients, with optional leek and chili for aroma without excess salt.
Serve hot with white rice, sprinkled with green onions or coriander. Serve with boiled vegetables or cucumber to balance the strong taste.
4 servings of braised dish eaten with rice in a family vegetarian meal.
Do not braise for too long after the eggplant is soft so that the eggplant pieces do not fall apart.
Choose firm eggplants, cut them and soak them in diluted salt water to limit browning.
Pan-frying or pan-frying the tofu helps the tofu retain its shape when braised.
Season with soy sauce slowly; The amount of stock reduces during cooking so you need to taste it at the end.
The center puffs soft and chewy while the thin rim spreads and crisps to a golden brown; mildly sweet with coconut aroma.

Bánh tai yến is a Mekong Delta snack with a flared rim resembling a bird’s nest, made with rice flour, tapioca starch, coconut milk and sugar. This Bếp Việt batch rests the batter before frying individual cakes.
Drain briefly and eat hot while the rim is crisp.
About 10 small cakes, best served hot.
About 4 hours 35 minutes, mostly batter resting time.
Rest the batter for about 4 hours, as described in the cultural reference.
Stir the batter before each scoop because flour may settle.
Pour a modest amount into hot oil so the rim flares and center puffs.

names: Khmer Ginger Cake from Sóc Trăng
fields: Ginger-root shapes have a crisp, airy shell with a white sugar coating and a sweet, rich rice-and-egg flavor.

Bánh gừng, called Num-khơ-nhây in Khmer, is a traditional Khmer Southern Vietnamese cake served during festivals, holidays and celebrations in Sóc Trăng. Sticky-rice flour and egg dough is shaped like ginger roots, fried and coated with sugar.
Let dry completely and serve with tea; store airtight in a dry place.
About 12 small ginger-shaped cakes coated with crystallized sugar.
About 1 hour 30 minutes, including draining and drying time.
Do not drop the cakes into very hot oil; it can harden them before they rise.
Fry until golden and firm, then drain before glazing.
Stir gently in the glaze until sugar turns white and crystallizes on the cakes.

names: Field Perch and Mustard Greens Soup
Field perch and mustard greens soup
Mustard greens soup with field perch
fields: Flaky perch and tender mustard greens sit in a light, ginger-scented broth.
Field perch and mustard greens soup
Mustard greens soup with field perch

A northern-style clear soup made with small field perch, mustard greens and ginger. The fish is simmered first and the strained cooking liquid becomes the broth, while the picked meat is returned to the pot.
Serve hot as part of a rice meal.
4 bowls of soup to share as part of a family rice meal.
Field Perch and Mustard Greens Soup
Strain the fish broth carefully and check the meat for pin bones.
Add greens near the end so they stay bright and tender.
Add the mustard greens to the simmering broth and cook briefly so they stay green and tender.

names: Pomelo salad with shrimp and pork belly
fields: Juicy shrimp and tender pork balance crisp pomelo, carrot and herbs under a bright sweet-sour dressing.
Pomelo salad with shrimp and pork belly

A light Vietnamese pomelo salad combines separated pomelo segments with boiled shrimp, sliced pork belly, carrot, Vietnamese coriander and a sweet-sour fish-sauce dressing. The dressing lightly coats the ingredients so the pomelo stays intact.
Plate and top with crushed roasted peanuts; serve immediately after mixing.
Four appetizer portions or a shared side dish.
Cool the cooked shrimp and pork completely before mixing.
Add dressing gradually and toss gently to keep pomelo segments whole.
Add the dressing a little at a time and toss just before serving so the pomelo segments keep their shape.
Tender chicken remains in pieces in a fragrant herbal broth; mugwort has a gentle bitterness and egg noodles stay springy.
Hanoi mì gà tần combines chicken braised with traditional herbal seasoning and mugwort, served with egg noodles. This Bếp Việt version adapts the street dish to a home pot with cut chicken pieces.
Blanch noodles separately, add chicken and mugwort, ladle over hot broth and finish with scallion and pepper.
Four bowls of egg noodles with herbal chicken, mugwort and broth.
About 1 hour 50 minutes, including 15 minutes to marinate the chicken.
Simmer the herb pack first so the broth is fragrant but not bitter.
Cook chicken until just tender; avoid over-braising.
Blanch noodles separately to keep the broth clear and noodles firm.

names: Mekong Delta Lá Mơ Cake with Coconut Sauce
fields: Green, chewy cake pieces are topped with rich coconut sauce and fragrant toasted sesame.

A soft, chewy Mekong Delta steamed cake gets its natural green color from lá mơ leaves and combines rice flour with tapioca starch. It is served with lightly thickened coconut sauce and toasted sesame.
Cut into pieces, pour over warm coconut sauce and sprinkle with sesame.
About 12 small steamed cake pieces with coconut sauce.
green herb steamed cake coconut sauce
Mekong Delta Lá Mơ Cake with Coconut Sauce
Strain the leaf juice finely for a smooth batter.
Stir continuously while heating the batter to prevent lumps.
Steam until the cakes are set and fully cooked; let them cool slightly before slicing to keep them from sticking to the knife.

names: Vegetarian Seitan Braised with Green Peppercorns
Vegetarian braised wheat gluten with green peppercorn
Wheat gluten braised with green peppercorn
fields: Seitan slices are browned and coated in a lightly reduced, savory-sweet coconut sauce with fragrant green peppercorns.
Vegetarian braised wheat gluten with green peppercorn
Wheat gluten braised with green peppercorn

Seitan is pan-seared, then braised with green peppercorns, soy sauce and fresh coconut water. This Bếp Việt vegetarian recipe uses Vietnamese leeks in place of shallots and keeps the sauce lightly reduced for serving with rice.
Serve hot with steamed rice and spoon the peppercorn sauce over the seitan.
Four portions of braised seitan served with hot rice.
mì căn kho tiêu xanh chay
Vegetarian Seitan Braised with Green Peppercorns
Pat seitan dry so it browns instead of steaming.
Check labels on sauces to ensure they suit your vegetarian diet.
Season lightly at first because the braising liquid will reduce; add the green peppercorns at the end to preserve their aroma.

names: Ca Mau Pandan Rice Cakes (Bánh Rây)
fields: Thin, soft and chewy cakes fragrant with pandan, with lightly sweet coconut and crunchy roasted peanuts.

Ca Mau bánh dứa, also called bánh rây, has a thin, soft glutinous-rice layer colored and scented with pandan. The batter is sifted directly into a hot pan, then folded with grated coconut and roasted peanuts. This fully plant-based home recipe is edited by Bếp Việt from the ingredients and method reported by Báo Cà Mau.
Fold each cake while warm and serve right away for the softest texture; add a little grated coconut and crushed peanuts if desired.
About 8 soft coconut-filled cakes, best while still warm.
About 50 minutes, including preparation and cooking.
Blend and strain the pandan thoroughly for a naturally green batter without fibers.
Keep the batter fluid enough to sift into a thin layer; stir before each cake because glutinous rice flour settles.
Cook over medium-low heat with the lid on for about 2 minutes so the cake steams through without dry edges.
Golden, crisp fritters with nutty mung beans and savory pork and shrimp, topped with a cooked shrimp.

Bánh cóng from Sóc Trăng is fried in a tall cylindrical mold called a cóng. A crisp rice-flour shell surrounds mung beans and a pork-and-shrimp filling, with a whole shrimp placed on top. Bếp Việt edited a home-size batch from Ngôi Sao (VnExpress) reporting on bánh cóng in Đại Tâm, Mỹ Xuyên.
Serve hot with lettuce, herbs, pickled vegetables and sweet-sour fish sauce.
About 8 small bánh cống fritters, served with greens and dipping sauce.
About 7 hours 10 minutes, including 6 hours for soaking the mung beans.
Soak the mung beans fully, then steam until tender but still holding their shape.
Preheat the mold in the frying oil so the fritter releases easily.
Use a moderate amount of filling and steady medium heat so the center cooks before the crust darkens.

names: Tra Vinh Bún Suông Noodle Soup
fields: A fragrant, savory-sweet broth with a gentle reddish-brown hue, tender springy shrimp suông, pork, shrimp and crisp fresh greens.

Bún suông from Trà Vinh is distinguished by springy shrimp paste shaped into long tapered pieces and poached in the broth. This Bếp Việt version combines shrimp paste with a tamarind and fermented-soybean broth described across the references; seasoning and toppings vary by household.
Divide the noodles among bowls, add suông, shrimp, pork and pork hock, then ladle over hot broth and sprinkle with scallions. Serve with greens, fermented soybean sauce or tamarind fish sauce.
4 full bowls with shrimp-paste suông, pork, shrimp and fresh vegetables.
About 2 hours 45 minutes, including a 1-hour chill for the shrimp paste.
Pat the peeled shrimp dry before pounding and mixing so the paste turns springy instead of loose.
Chill the shrimp paste before shaping to help the suông hold its tapered form in the broth.
Simmer the broth gently and skim it often for a clean, naturally sweet flavor.
Clear, naturally sweet broth with tender pork rind, fragrant pork and dried shrimp, and colorful vegetables that retain a slight crispness.

Canh bóng thả is a delicate soup served in old-style Hanoi Tết feasts. Chicken stock is blended with the cooking liquids from dried shrimp and pork tenderloin; pork rind and vegetables are cooked just until tender so they keep their color and gentle bite.
Arrange the pork rind, vegetables, tenderloin and dried shrimp in bowls. Pour over piping-hot broth and finish with cilantro and pepper.
4 bowls of light soup with pork rind, pork tenderloin, dried shrimp and vegetables.
About 3 hours, including 60–90 minutes to soak the pork rind.
Soak the pork rind in concentrated glutinous-rice washing water until expanded, then deodorize it with ginger and rice wine and rinse well.
Skim the stock as it simmers and remove excess fat for a clear, delicate soup.
Heat the pork rind only until tender; long cooking can make it soft and limp.

names: Phu Tho Bánh Tai Rice Dumplings
fields: Soft, slightly chewy white rice dough folded into curved half moons around a moist, peppery pork and shallot filling.

Bánh tai is a savory everyday dumpling from Phú Thọ town: soft, chewy rice dough encloses pork shoulder seasoned with shallot, pepper and fish sauce, then is shaped into a curved ear-like half moon and steamed. Bếp Việt edited this family batch from the process introduced by the Phú Thọ Tourism Information and Promotion Center.
Serve hot as soon as the dumplings leave the steamer; pair with lightly seasoned fish sauce or pickled vegetables.
About 12 small steamed bánh tai dumplings, served hot.
About 4 hours 10 minutes, including a 3-hour rice soak.
Thi Xa Phu Tho banh tai
Soak the rice long enough for fine milling; add cold water gradually while kneading so the dough does not become too wet.
Pound and knead the dough while warm until smooth, pliable and free of cracks.
Shape a gentle curve and avoid overfilling so the seam stays closed while steaming.
A firm, chewy amber cake with fragrant rice and ginger notes and a sesame topping; once cool, it is firm enough to slice.

Banh to is a sweet sticky rice cake associated with Tet in Quang Nam. Sources describe glutinous rice, block cane sugar, ginger and sesame, steamed in a banana-leaf-lined mold. This is a small home batch using ready-ground glutinous rice flour and a shorter steaming time suited to a home mold; its proportions are not presented as a local bakery's formula.
Let the cake cool and firm before slicing. Eat it soft or pan-fry the slices in a little oil until the outside turns golden.
One round cake about 18 cm across, cut into 10–12 thin slices.
About 4 hours 25 minutes, including steaming and cooling until firm.
steamed cake with block cane sugar
Let the syrup cool slightly before mixing it into the flour to prevent lumps.
Line the mold bottom completely with banana leaf and leave a little headroom for the cake to expand.
Keep the steamer water at a steady simmer and top it up with hot water if needed during the long steam.
A fragrant roll with pepper and banana-leaf aromas, a smooth rosy-brown interior and a savory, gently springy beef texture.

Da Nang's tourism portal describes chả bò as a local beef sausage made with trimmed beef thigh, finely ground and seasoned with onion, garlic, pepper, chili, sugar and fish sauce, then wrapped in banana leaves and boiled. Bếp Việt has adapted a small home batch, keeping the beef cold while grinding and forming two short rolls so they cook evenly.
Let the sausage cool slightly before slicing. Serve with pickled vegetables, herbs, baguette or beef porridge.
Two small sausage rolls, about 600 g total, sliced and served with pickles or baguette.
About 1 hour 35 minutes, including a short cooling rest after boiling.
Chill the beef, grinder bowl and water before grinding so the meat stays cold and cohesive.
Wrap two short rolls tightly and seal the leaves so water cannot seep inside.
Use a clean food thermometer to confirm the center of the sausage reaches 71°C before removing it from the pot.

names: Ca Mau Ốc Len with Coconut
fields: The cooked snails are springy and fragrant with lemongrass and garlic, coated in a lightly sweet and savory coconut sauce finished with Vietnamese coriander.

Ốc len snails live in mangrove forests and coastal mudflats in Ca Mau. Local reporting describes soaking them to release grit, cutting the pointed tail, then cooking them with coconut milk, garlic, lemongrass and Vietnamese coriander. Bếp Việt has edited a home batch using snails from a reliable food supplier and cooking them thoroughly.
Serve hot in a shallow bowl with the coconut sauce. Bread can be used to mop up the sauce.
One hot plate of snails for four people to share as a snack or starter.
About 1 hour 30 minutes, mostly for soaking the snails to release grit.
Ca Mau oc len with coconut
Choose live snails with intact shells; discard dead snails or any with an off smell before soaking.
Cut just enough of the pointed tail to open the shell for suction; do not cut so deeply that the snail breaks apart.
Cook at a steady simmer until the snails are fully cooked; discard shells that remain closed or smell unusual.

names: Beef Offal in Coconut and Five-Spice Broth
fields: Tender but slightly springy offal absorbs five-spice and coconut; the amber broth smells of ginger, star anise and cinnamon.
Beef Offal in Coconut and Five-Spice Broth

Beef pha lau is a familiar street food in Ho Chi Minh City. Sources describe beef offal cleaned carefully, seasoned with five-spice and aromatics, then simmered in coconut water. Bếp Việt has adapted a home-size batch with commonly available beef tripe, cooked until tender and served with baguette, Vietnamese coriander and a sweet-sour dipping sauce.
Cut the offal into bite-size pieces and ladle over hot broth. Serve with crisp baguette, Vietnamese coriander and a lime dipping sauce.
Four small bowls of pha lau, served with baguette and Vietnamese coriander.
About 2 hours 40 minutes, including a 30-minute marinade before braising.
Rub the offal with ginger, vinegar and rice wine, then rinse thoroughly before blanching.
Brief blanching and rinsing reduce strong aromas without over-tightening the offal before braising.
Simmer gently until the thickest pieces are tender; taste after the coconut broth reduces because its saltiness becomes more concentrated.
Soft millet grains blend with mashed mung beans into a thick golden porridge with gentle sweetness; crisp sesame crackers add contrast.

Hoi An heritage records include millet sweet porridge among the offerings for the Doan Ngo festival. A recipe presented with guidance from a culinary artisan combines millet and mung beans and serves the porridge with toasted rice crackers for scooping. Bếp Việt has edited a plant-based batch without dairy or animal fat, cooked until thick enough to eat by spoon or with rice crackers.
Spoon the warm or cooled porridge into small bowls. Break toasted sesame rice crackers into pieces to scoop it up.
Four thick bowls of sweet porridge with toasted sesame rice crackers.
About 2 hours 5 minutes, including 1 hour for soaking the millet and mung beans.
Soak millet and mung beans separately so both soften evenly.
Stir gently but regularly once the millet thickens so it does not stick to the pot.
Add the sugar after the mung beans soften so you can adjust sweetness and thickness easily.

names: Mekong Delta Sesbania Flower Bánh Xèo
fields: Thin golden crepes with crisp edges, just-cooked shrimp and pork, bean sprouts and intact sesbania flowers; fresh greens and tamarind sauce balance the gentle richness.

Sesbania flower bánh xèo is associated with the Mekong Delta flood season, when the yellow blossoms are placed in the filling rather than served only as a side green. Bếp Việt edits a home batch with shrimp, pork belly, bean sprouts and seasonal sesbania flowers; a light coconut mixture makes the crepe fragrant while keeping it crisp. Use only flowers sold as food from a safe source, wash them well and drain thoroughly.
Serve hot. Break off a piece, wrap it with lettuce and herbs, then dip it in tamarind fish sauce. Do not stack the crepes for long, as trapped steam softens the crust.
About eight medium crepes, two per person, served with fresh greens and tamarind fish sauce.
About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 20 minutes for the batter to rest; frying time varies with pan size.
Rest the batter for 20 minutes, then stir again; if it is thick, add water a little at a time so it spreads thinly.
Dry the sesbania flowers after washing to reduce oil splatter and keep the crepes crisp.
Cover briefly to cook the filling, then uncover and keep the heat moderate until the edges dry and crisp.
Evenly cooked sticky rice in bamboo tubes, glossy and tender with a light roasted-bamboo aroma; serve with nutty sesame salt.

Cơm lam is a way of cooking glutinous rice in bamboo or reed tubes over a fire and is recorded across several Northwest provinces. Bếp Việt edits a home batch with overnight-soaked upland sticky rice, a little salt and ginger; the rice cooks tender and fragrant inside the young bamboo membrane. Families and local areas differ in seasoning, tube choice and accompaniments.

Let the tubes cool slightly, peel away the outer bamboo and keep the thin inner membrane attached to the rice. Cut into serving pieces and eat with sesame salt; grilled stream fish or pork can be served alongside.
Four small bamboo tubes, one per person; serve with sesame salt or grilled dishes.
About 9 hours 10 minutes, including overnight rice soaking; grilling time varies with tube size and coal heat.
what to serve with cơm lam
Soak and drain the rice well so it cooks evenly without a hard center.
Fill the tubes only about two-thirds full and leave room for the rice to expand.
Turn the tubes regularly over glowing coals; one side can char before the rice cooks if left facing the heat.
A hot bowl of thick, pleasantly chewy noodles with sweet crab meat and a clean, seafood-forward broth topped with a little scallion and cilantro.

Bánh canh ghẹ is a familiar seafood noodle soup in Vũng Tàu; its broth is commonly simmered with crab and pork bones for a rounded natural sweetness. Bếp Việt edits a home version with thick bánh canh noodles, blue swimmer crab, shallot and a little annatto oil for a warm, clear broth.
Place the noodles in bowls and ladle over boiling broth. Add the crab meat, claws, scallion and cilantro. Serve hot with pepper, lime and chili to taste.
Four medium bowls, each with one portion of crab and thick noodles.
About 1 hour 15 minutes for prep, broth and crab; fresh noodles shorten the cooking time.
Choose fresh crabs with intact shells; steaming them separately keeps the meat from breaking down in the broth.
Skim the pork-bone broth as it simmers for a clearer, cleaner flavor.
Blanch the noodles separately if they have excess surface starch, so the soup does not become too thick.

names: Krông Pa One-Sun Beef with Ant-Egg Salt
One-sun beef with muối kiến vàng
fields: Warm one-sun beef with lightly charred edges and tender slices inside; muối kiến vàng adds savory, tangy, spicy and aromatic notes.
One-sun beef with muối kiến vàng

One-sun beef served with muối kiến vàng is a regional pairing associated with Krông Pa, Gia Lai and Central Highlands food culture. The beef is seasoned and dried in the sun for a day before it is cooked for serving; this Bếp Việt home version uses commercially prepared, labeled one-sun beef, quickly grilled and served with food-grade ant-egg salt.
Rest the beef for 3 minutes, then slice across the grain. Serve with muối kiến vàng, herbs or rice paper, following the package's storage and cooking instructions.
One 500 g plate of prepared beef to share with vegetables and rice paper for 3–4 people.
About 22 minutes using prepared one-sun beef; the traditional seasoning and sun-drying time is not part of this reheating recipe.
Choose labeled one-sun beef with a clear use-by date and storage directions; thaw in the refrigerator if frozen.
Preheat the grill and cook briefly on each side; prolonged grilling makes the meat dry and tough.
Muối kiến vàng may contain insect allergens; check ingredients and avoid it if you have a related allergy.

names: Quảng Bình Cháo Canh with Snakehead Fish
fields: Thick, tender noodles in a hot broth with lightly turmeric-colored snakehead fish and just-cooked mustard greens; the broth is gently thickened, not like rice porridge.

Cháo canh is a rustic specialty of Quảng Bình. Despite the word cháo, the dish is a noodle soup made with thick wheat- or rice-flour noodles, snakehead fish, meat and mustard greens. Bếp Việt edits a fish version with pork-bone stock, củ nén and turmeric; fresh noodles are used to simplify the home preparation.
Serve while piping hot with scallion and black pepper. Crispy ram rolls can accompany the bowl as they do in local servings; add chili if desired.
Four medium bowls, each with thick dough noodles, snakehead fish and mustard greens.
About 1 hour 5 minutes with fresh noodles; cooking time varies with the noodle type.
Choose fresh or packaged cháo canh noodles and follow the package cooking time so they do not break down.
Cook the fish just until done, remove all bones carefully and strain the poaching liquid for a clean broth.
Add the mustard greens at the end; once the broth returns to a boil, turn off the heat to keep the greens bright and crisp.
Each warm cake has a neat slender shape, a tender ivory rice casing and a savory pork filling with lightly crisp mushrooms and fragrant shallots.

Phu Nhi rice cakes are a Xu Doai specialty made from wet-ground rice batter and filled with pork, wood-ear mushrooms and shallots before being wrapped in leaves and boiled. Bếp Việt adapts the traditional technique for a small home batch, stirring the batter until smooth and pliable without letting it become pasty.
Unwrap while warm and enjoy with pickled vegetables or a little dipping sauce. Re-steam briefly if the cakes cool; avoid boiling them again, which can make the casing waterlogged.
About eight slender cakes, two per person, served warm with a light dipping sauce.
About 4 hours 35 minutes, including three hours to soak the rice; the rice can be soaked overnight.
Vietnamese pork rice cakes in leaves
Soak the rice until soft, then blend it thoroughly; strain if any coarse grains remain.
Stir the batter over low heat until just thickened and still pliable. Overcooked batter is difficult to spread around the filling.
Wrap the leaves snugly but leave room for expansion, then tie gently so the cakes cook evenly without splitting.

names: Shrimp and pork bánh ram ít
fields: A golden crisp base supports a tender ivory dumpling with savory shrimp and pork, a little scallion oil and a gentle chili-lime dip.
Shrimp and pork bánh ram ít

Hue bánh ram ít combines two textures in one bite: a soft glutinous-rice dumpling filled with shrimp and pork, set on a crisp fried rice base. Bếp Việt edits a home-sized batch with lightly seasoned filling and a sweet-sour fish sauce for serving.
Assemble each dumpling on its crispy base just before serving. Eat warm with lightly sweetened garlic-chili fish sauce to balance the richness and chewiness.
About twelve small dumplings, three per person, served while the crispy bases are fresh.
About 1 hour 35 minutes, including a 15-minute dough rest; fry the bases in small batches to keep them crisp.
Add warm water to the glutinous-rice flour gradually until the dough is smooth and not sticky.
Steam the bases first, let them cool and pat dry before frying to make them crisp with less splatter.
Cook the filling until fairly dry and let it cool before wrapping so the dough does not become soggy.
A pale-golden coconut broth carries the natural sweetness of pumpkin and root vegetables. Each piece of vegetable, mushroom and tofu skin stays distinct, creating a gently rich plant-based soup.

Canh kiểm is a Southern Vietnamese vegetarian soup that simmers a variety of vegetables in coconut liquid and is often served at vegetarian meals and offerings. Bếp Việt edits a home version with pumpkin, sweet potato, taro, green banana, long beans, mushrooms, tofu skin and peanuts; the ingredients are added in stages so tender vegetables keep their shape.
Serve hot with rice or vermicelli. Ladle gently so the vegetables stay intact; if using thick coconut cream, dilute it to keep the broth from becoming heavy.
One pot of about 1.5 litres, served with steamed rice or fresh rice vermicelli.
Vietnamese vegetarian pumpkin and taro soup
Briefly pan-sear the taro to help it hold its shape and develop a nutty flavor.
Add pumpkin and long beans after the slower-cooking roots so they do not overcook.
Use coconut milk in moderation and season at the end, since the vegetables vary in natural sweetness.

names: Mushroom and tofu bún in Hue style
fields: A hot bowl with clear lemongrass-scented broth, gentle mushroom sweetness, golden tofu, tender chewy wheat gluten and green vegetables makes a light but satisfying meal.
Mushroom and tofu bún in Hue style

Hue vegetarian bún is a fragrant noodle soup built around mushrooms and lemongrass, served with rice vermicelli, fried tofu, wheat gluten, bamboo shoots and greens. Bếp Việt edits a fully plant-based home version with a vegetable-and-mushroom broth; check packaged seasonings to avoid animal-derived ingredients.

Blanch the noodles separately, place them in bowls, then ladle over the simmering broth with mushrooms, bamboo shoots, tofu and wheat gluten. Add herbs, pepper or chili and serve at once so the noodles stay springy.
Four generous bowls with mushrooms, tofu, bamboo shoots and wheat gluten.
About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 20 minutes to soak bamboo shoots and mushrooms; pre-cooked fresh bamboo shoots shorten the preparation.
Boil dried bamboo shoots twice, changing the water, and taste them before cooking to reduce bitterness and strong aromas.
Sauté the mushrooms and wheat gluten before adding them to deepen the flavor of both the toppings and broth.
Use leek in place of onion and garlic if desired, and verify that packaged seasoning is fully plant-based.
Each small square cake has a glossy dark casing with the fragrance of ramie leaves, a sweet mung-bean and coconut center, a hint of molasses and a lightly nutty sesame finish.

Tu Tru bánh gai from Mia village in Tho Xuan is known for a dark glutinous-rice casing made with ramie leaves, a mung-bean and coconut filling, gentle molasses sweetness and sesame. Bếp Việt adapts a small batch with softened dried ramie leaves and ordinary home equipment; the parcels are wrapped in banana leaf, steamed and cooled so the casing becomes pleasantly chewy.
Let the cakes cool completely before peeling the inner leaf, since the casing is sticky. Serve in small pieces with hot tea; briefly steam again if a refrigerated cake becomes firm.
About eight small cakes, two per person, served cooled with hot tea.
About 4 hours 25 minutes, including three hours to soak the mung beans and ramie leaves; these can be soaked ahead.
Vietnamese mung bean coconut ramie cake
Cook the ramie leaves until very soft, then blend or pound finely; fibrous leaves make the casing rough.
Cook the filling until it just holds together when rolled; drying it too much makes the center crumbly.
Wrap the parcels securely and steam over steady medium heat. Let them dry and cool before stacking so condensation does not collect on the leaves.

names: Bac Lieu spicy beef rice noodles
fields: A hot bowl of naturally golden-orange broth, tender but distinct beef slices, white vermicelli and fragrant Thai basil; add satay and chili separately to control the heat.

Bac Lieu spicy beef bún is known for its deep golden broth, the fragrant heat of satay and tender beef served with white rice vermicelli. Bếp Việt adapts a home batch with a lighter broth, keeping Thai basil, lime and chili salt as characteristic accompaniments.
Briefly blanch the noodles, arrange the beef and ladle over simmering broth. Serve with Thai basil, lime and chili salt; let each person add satay at the table.
Four medium bowls with spicy broth, beef and Thai basil; adjust the satay to taste.
About 2 hours 15 minutes, mostly for simmering the bones and tenderizing the beef.
Blanch the bones and beef briefly, then rinse them to reduce scum and odor in the broth.
Fry the satay gently and use enough for aroma and color without letting the chili burn.
Remove the beef as soon as tender, cool slightly and slice across the grain; keep the broth at a gentle simmer.

names: Black bánh chưng from Xu Lang
fields: A square cake with glossy dark glutinous rice, a nutty yellow mung-bean layer and tender pork; the color comes from the rice treatment, not charring.
Black bánh chưng from Xu Lang

Lang Son black bánh chưng is a Tay variation: glutinous rice is soaked in carefully filtered plant-ash water, then wrapped with mung beans and pork in dong leaves. Bếp Việt adapts a family batch; use only ash water confirmed safe for food and never burn unknown plants to make it.
Let the cake rest after boiling, press it lightly to drain, then slice with a clean knife. Serve with pickled onions or vegetables; refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat thoroughly.
One family-sized square cake cut into eight pieces; serve warm or pan-fry after refrigeration.
About 20 hours, including eight hours of soaking and 10–12 hours of boiling; the rice can soak overnight.
black glutinous rice cake with mung bean and pork
soaking rice in food-grade ash water
Use only plant-ash water labeled or confirmed for food use; do not use ash from unidentified plants, contaminated materials or chemical-treated wood.
Soak the rice and mung beans separately and distribute the filling evenly so the center cooks through.
Keep the cake submerged during boiling, top up with boiling water and maintain a gentle boil; never let the pot run dry.

names: Steamed red tilapia with ginger and scallions
Ginger and scallion steamed red tilapia
fields: The thickest flesh is opaque and flakes easily while remaining moist; ginger and scallions are aromatic, with a lightly glossy sauce.
Ginger and scallion steamed red tilapia

Red tilapia stays moist and tender, scented with ginger and scallions in a gently seasoned sauce. This Bếp Việt family version keeps the sauce measured and serves the steaming juices with rice or noodles.
Set the fish on a deep platter, spoon over the sauce and juices, and finish with fried shallots and herbs. Serve with rice or rice vermicelli.
One 800–900 g red tilapia steamed with ginger and scallions for four people.
About 75 minutes including a 10-minute marinade; steaming depends on size and thickness.
steamed red tilapia with ginger and scallions
món cá hấp cho bữa cơm
Preheat the steamer and bring the water to a boil before adding the fish.
Check that the thickest section reaches 63°C or is opaque and flakes easily; avoid oversteaming.
Tender but intact pumpkin, lightly coated with fragrant garlic and finished with cilantro.

Pumpkin is quickly stir-fried with garlic, then covered briefly with a little water until just tender. The pieces stay intact and retain their naturally sweet, nutty flavor, making a simple weeknight vegetable side.
Transfer to a plate, scatter with cilantro and serve hot with steamed rice.
One family-style plate of stir-fried pumpkin with garlic for four people.
About 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
Cut pumpkin evenly and add water a little at a time.
Cover briefly over low heat and stop cooking once tender.
A bowl of translucent glass noodles in golden broth, topped with golden eel, scallions and Vietnamese coriander.

Nghệ An eel glass-noodle soup combines glass noodles and freshwater eel with a turmeric-scented pork-bone broth and local shallots. Bếp Việt serves the eel in two textures: a lightly coated crisp portion and a soft sautéed portion.
Soften the glass noodles, divide them among bowls and arrange the crispy and sautéed eel on top. Pour over hot broth and finish with scallions, Vietnamese coriander and pepper.
Four bowls of eel glass noodles with bone broth, crispy eel and sautéed eel.
About 1 hour and 45 minutes, including broth simmering and noodle soaking.
Clean the eel thoroughly and remove any bones before serving.
Use only a thin flour coating so the fried eel stays crisp without becoming heavy.
Soak glass noodles according to the package and blanch separately to keep the broth clear.

names: Nha Trang rice cakes with shrimp and quail eggs
Nha Trang bánh căn with shrimp and quail eggs
fields: Small cakes with lightly golden edges and soft centers, topped with shrimp or quail egg and served hot with scallion oil, fresh herbs, green mango and fish sauce.
Nha Trang bánh căn with shrimp and quail eggs
